questions.label: Q8
questions.question: Should the schedule store a full hire spec, prefilled from the source worker when it comes from a suggestion?
questions.context: The hire needs floor, desk, harness/model/effort, cwd, and the worktree flag. The sub-questions are what to do if a stored worktree cwd has disappeared by fire time and what the worktree default should be; the desk is picked at fire time, not stored.
questions.recommendation: Store the full spec (floor, harness, model, effort, cwd, worktree), prefilled from the source worker and editable. If the stored cwd has disappeared at fire time, fall back to the worktree's repo root plus `worktree: true` (fresh `h3d/` branch). Default `worktree: false` when the source wasn't a worktree, otherwise as above.

questions.label: Q9
questions.question: What should happen if the floor is asleep when the schedule fires?
options: (b) Mark the schedule `failed: floor_asleep` and notify.
(c) Add a per-schedule “wake floor if asleep” checkbox, default on.
questions.context: `floor.wake` resumes every worker on the floor, which is a side effect.
questions.recommendation: (c), default on. The whole point is not having to remember. Resuming the floor's other workers is acceptable collateral, and users who object can turn it off.

questions.label: Q10
questions.question: What should happen if desks are full when the schedule fires?
options: (b) Wait in a `waiting_desk` state until a desk frees, shown in the display, with “run now” still available; count this toward lateness under `max_lateness`.
questions.recommendation: (b). A soak follow-up running an hour late beats one that never runs.

questions.label: Q11
questions.question: How should the handoff reach the new agent?
options: (a) Inline the handoff text into the prompt.
(b) Append “Context from earlier session: read `~/handoff/<floor>/<file>.md` first” to the explicit prompt.
questions.context: The prompt limit is 32 KiB and a handoff can be larger.
questions.recommendation: (b). Size-safe, the file is already on the bridge host, and it reuses the handoff as-is. If the file was deleted before firing, run without it and add a note to the prompt.

questions.label: Q12
questions.question: How should handoff sources work when creating a schedule?
questions.context: For schedules created from a suggestion chip, decide whether to auto-create a literal handoff of the source message when saved, with a checkbox to opt out. For manual creation, decide whether to offer an optional picker for existing handoffs or allow none. Also decide whether to offer LLM/agent handoff modes.
questions.recommendation: Chip: literal handoff, checkbox on by default. Manual: optional picker over existing handoffs. Literal only in this epic; the user can make an LLM handoff separately first and then pick it.

questions.label: Q13
questions.question: Should schedule suggestions use a separate settings toggle or share the follow-ups toggle, and what should its default be?
options: Separate bridge setting, off by default.
questions.context: The proposal reuses the follow-ups (#90) turn-end hook with a second classifier question and extracts `{due_at, draft_prompt, title}`, using the current time in UTC and the user's timezone. Use the same 0.7 gate and once-per-message dedup; show no chip if the LLM can't produce a concrete `due_at`.
questions.recommendation: A separate bridge setting, “Schedule suggestions”, off by default like follow-ups, with the same 0.7 gate and the same once-per-message dedup. If the LLM can't produce a concrete `due_at`, show no chip.

questions.label: Q14
questions.question: Which office display form should schedules use?
options: (a) Per-floor board showing only that floor's schedules.
(b) A single global board in the lobby/lounge.
(c) Per-floor board, with an “all floors” toggle in the dialog.
questions.context: The proposed board shows the next ~3 schedules with countdowns; clicking it opens a HUD dialog with the full list and create/edit/cancel/run-now actions.
questions.recommendation: (c). Schedules belong to a floor (that's where they hire), but the overview needs to cover all floors.

questions.label: Q15
questions.question: Where should users be able to create a schedule without a chip?
options: “Schedule follow-up…” on any transcript message only.
Both the display dialog's “+ New” and “Schedule follow-up…” on any transcript message.
questions.context: The transcript-message entry point is next to Handoff, even for unclassified messages, and reuses the chip's prefill path minus the LLM draft.
questions.recommendation: The first two. The second reuses the chip's prefill path minus the LLM draft. No shortcut for now.

questions.label: Q16
questions.question: How should users hear about a schedule firing, running late, being skipped, or failing?
options: Game toast plus display status; no OS-level push notification in this epic.
questions.context: The hired worker appearing at a desk is also a signal.
questions.recommendation: Game toast plus display status. The hired worker appearing at a desk is the main signal. No OS-level push in this epic.

questions.label: Q17
questions.question: What grace period should define when a schedule counts as missed?
questions.context: The proposal is a wall-clock check every 30 seconds rather than one long monotonic timer, plus a check on startup. A schedule is missed when first checked more than the grace period after `due_at`; then the `on_miss` policy applies.
questions.recommendation: 5 min grace. Under that it just runs, with no late note. The scan on startup covers a bridge restart.
